title: Autonomous host swapline with traffic-shed and preheat
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Introduce an autonomous host replacement pipeline ("swapline") that performs scheduled swapping of hosts in Dedicated fleets while preserving throughput guarantees. The swapline should incrementally shed traffic from the source host, preheat destination hosts (KV cache and model warm-up), and hand off steady-state traffic with automatic rollback if SLOs degrade. This work ties together autoscaling policies, capacity reservations, and maintenance windows for predictable capacity during planned replacements.
acceptance_criteria: Swapline can replace a host without exceeding p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs for >99% of requests during the operation
Destination host preheat completes (KV cache seeded + model context warm-up) prior to crossing 50% traffic handoff
Automated rollback triggers if error rate or p99 latency increases beyond configured thresholds for 2 consecutive minutes
Integration tests that simulate replacement under typical and burst traffic pass in CI (see linked PR)
Metrics surfaced in Console: swapline duration, handoff progress, preheat time, rollback events, capacity reserved
implementation_plan: Design swapline controller that coordinates: drain orchestration, preheat orchestrator, traffic shed algorithm, and rollback detector
Extend autoscaler to temporarily reserve throughput lanes (soft reservations) for destination hosts during handoff
Implement a lightweight preheat runner that issues synthetic warm requests and seeds KV cache using recent request prefixes
Add traffic-shed policy that offloads incremental percent of connections with constraints from routing layer
Create observability surface in Console and alerting rules (rollback, slow preheat, handoff stalls)
Develop integration tests and chaos scenarios (node replacement under 1x, 2x, and 3x baseline load), and add to smoke-suite
Run staged rollout to Dedicated fleets with Canary traffic at 1%, 5%, 20% before full enablement
tradeoffs: Preheating increases short-term token cost due to synthetic requests but reduces long-tail latency spikes when traffic is moved
Soft capacity reservations reduce burst headroom temporarily and could increase autoscale churn; we limit reservation window to avoid long-term impact
More aggressive traffic-shed reduces time-to-swap but increases immediate p99 risk; chosen default favors conservative increments with operator override
